Report for Monday, Nov 9, 2026 (ET) · new items since the Nov 2 report · Ascendancy Final Frontier: 3 latest Gamefound updates · sections sorted by newest story · Past reports

18 games 59 stories 7 status checks 7 new this week Facts only Gold tag = older but still relevant

This week at a glance

  • StarCraft TMG (Nov 7): Disputed “Wave 4 leak” images show an Alarak vs. Stukov starter and a Firebat box. The community is split on whether they are real, and Archon has not commented. Fans expect Wave 4 pre-orders around Nov 16.
  • Blood Rage: Valhalla: The U.S. retail date of Nov 6 has passed and the base game is still orderable at Asmodee USA. The Road to Helheim expansion now shows Sold out there.
  • Dice Throne Nexus: The Kickstarter closed Nov 3. The page now shows $2,236,007 from 15,611 backers, and a BackerKit pledge manager follows.
  • Dune: Imperium – Conspiracy (Nov 3): Design Diary 2 explains raids, a new way to spend swords on planet rewards. A Leaders diary is next.
  • Marvel Champions: Elektra and Iron Fist are still dated Nov 13 at Asmodee USA; Asmodee UK lists Elektra for Nov 20. A Critical Encounters podcast (Nov 5) recaps the MC/DC 2026 fan convention.
  • Star Wars stock (Nov 9): The Imperial Assault Core Set is still in stock at Asmodee USA; the Rebellion core set is still Sold out. Neither has an out-of-print notice.
  • Star Trek Ascendancy: Final Frontier: The latest three Gamefound updates are still #48 (Oct 5, Unboxing! Shipping Imminent!), #47 (Aug 28), and #46 (Aug 21). There was no Update 49 on Nov 9.
  • Special watch: Marvel Legendary What If…? Season 2: No change. There is still no official Upper Deck status post, and a Canadian pre-order listing remains live.

StarCraft Miniatures Game

StarCraft: Tabletop Miniatures Game · Archon Studio (Blizzard license)

Community: disputed “Wave 4 leak” images show an Alarak vs. Stukov starter and a Firebat box; Archon has not commented

Nov 7, 2026 (community) New this week

Two images posted on r/StarCraftTMG on the night of Nov 5–6 appear to show a Wave 4 two-player starter called Purification (Tal’darim with Alarak against “Stukov’s Forces” with infested marines, an infested missile turret, a Defiler, and an infested Goliath) plus a Terran Firebat box with six Firebats and a flame-wall marker. The images carry the Archon logo, but players are split: some say Archon’s Discord called them an AI fake, others say the consensus there is that they are real. Fan site sc-tabletop-news.de notes that a Siege Tank shown on the October AMA roadmap is missing from the starter picture.

Nothing here is confirmed. As of Nov 7 Archon had not commented, and starcraft-tmg.com’s newest news post is still the Oct 19 Terran preview. A community summary of the October AMA says Wave 4 pre-orders should open on Nov 16. Separately, the same site reported on Nov 4 that r/StarCraftTMG users are posting more Wave 3 mispacks (duplicate or missing sprues) and that replacement tickets can take weeks. Archon’s published schedule had Wave 3 shipping from Nov 2 in Europe and from Nov 9 for the rest of the world.

Sources: sc-tabletop-news.de (Nov 7) · sc-tabletop-news.de front page (Nov 4 mispack report) · starcraft-tmg.com news

Oct 29, 2026 Carried forward · last week

Sources: Archon Studio blog (Oct 29) · Official pre-order post (Oct 9)

Wave 3 Terran rules preview: Raven (first flying-stand unit) and two Nova Terra loadouts

Oct 19, 2026 Older · still relevant

Archon Studio’s Oct 19 development post previews the Terran half of Wave 3. The Raven is described as the game’s first airborne unit on a dedicated flight stand: a support drone built around an Advanced Sensor Array (detection), automated deployment systems, and target painting rather than front-line damage. Nova Terra is a Hero with two loadouts: Stealth Mode (C-20A Canister Rifle, Stealth Suit, long-range picks) and Assault Mode (Hellfire Shotgun and Monomolecular Blade for close combat).

This completes a three-post series this week covering every Wave 3 faction (Zerg Oct 14, Protoss Oct 16, Terran Oct 19). Pre-orders opened Oct 12; official shipping starts Nov 2 (Europe) and Nov 9 (rest of world).

Sources: Archon blog (Oct 19) · StarCraft TMG rules post

Wave 3 Protoss rules preview: Tassadar’s Force Walls and the High Templar

Oct 16, 2026 Older · still relevant

Archon’s Oct 16 post covers the Protoss Wave 3 additions. Tassadar is a support Hero focused on board control: Force Walls block movement paths and can inflict damage that bypasses armour rolls when enemies move through or around them. Khala’s Gift reduces the cost of a friendly Biological unit’s first Special Ability each round, and Executor’s Will lets him mark two enemy units in the Assault Phase. The post also previews the High Templar unit.

Sources: Archon blog (Oct 16) · StarCraft TMG rules post

Wave 3 Zerg rules preview: Defiler (Dark Swarm, Consume, Plague), Zagara, and a Bile Launcher structure

Oct 14, 2026 Older · still relevant

Archon’s Oct 14 post details the Zerg side. The Defiler (40 mm base) brings Dark Swarm (a token that lets nearby friendly units make evade rolls in the assault phase, with +1 for size-one units), Consume (destroy a nearby friendly model to cut biomass costs), and Plague (a blast template of non-lethal damage that scales with biomass spent). Broodmother Zagara grants a once-per-round bonus to units of a chosen size and can use her base as an entry edge (Infested Drop).

Zagara’s box also includes a Bile Launcher: a placeable artillery structure (within 18″ of your entry edge) with Bombard that does not need line of sight. Archon says it is the first structure that can hold objective markers. A Zagara’s Swarm faction card and a Reactive Creep card are also included.

Sources: Archon blog (Oct 14) · StarCraft TMG rules post

October 2026 balance changelog: Terran Stimpack units cost more, Zerg infantry cheaper

Changelog dated Oct 9, 2026 Older · still relevant

Archon’s official changelog dated 09.10.2026 (not covered in last week’s report) adjusts unit and tactical-card costs “to encourage greater variety in army compositions,” with “particular attention to Zerg.” Terran: Marine (160/210 → 170/220), Marauder, Medic (110 → 120), and Jim Raynor (250 → 280) go up; Barracks and Academy cost more gas; Dropship and Goliath get cheaper. Zerg: Zergling (180/220 → 150/210), Raptor, Swarmling (260 → 210), Queen, Roach variants, Hydralisk upgrades, and several tactical cards get cheaper. Protoss: Zealot, Adept, Artanis, and Nexus go up; Praetor Guard, Stalker, Sentry upgrades, and Twilight Council go down.

A matching October 2026 cost table is posted on the official downloads page.

Sources: Changelog PDF (Oct 9) · Cost table PDF · Official downloads page

Dune Imperium

Dire Wolf · Imperium / Uprising / Immortality and related expansions

Conspiracy Design Diary 2: raids let you spend swords on planets instead of the Conflict

Nov 3, 2026 New this week

Dire Wolf’s second Dune: Imperium – Conspiracy diary (Corey Burkhart, Nov 3) explains raids. On your Reveal turn you can spend sword icons (not unit strength) on raid tokens, which are planets that give resources, and put the rest of your swords into the Conflict. Each player can take up to five raids. The second and fourth raids cost you a rank with a Faction of your choice; the third and fifth let you flip an earlier raid face-down and collect its reward again.

Raid tokens come in two pools: bronze (one to three swords) and blue (two to five). The diary also previews Unstoppable Crusade, War Veteran, and Victory Plaza, and mentions the two-sword Conspirator reserve card. A diary on Leaders is next. Pre-orders remain open on Dire Wolf’s web store.

Sources: Dire Wolf Design Diary 2 (Nov 3) · Dire Wolf shop

Conspiracy pre-orders open on Dire Wolf’s shop ($40); first Design Diary explains Conspiracy cards

Oct 26, 2026 · shop rechecked Nov 2 Carried forward · last week

Dire Wolf’s Oct 26 Design Diary by Paul Dennen says Dune: Imperium – Conspiracy is now available for pre-order. Players draft four Conspiracy cards at setup (draw five, keep one, pass the rest). Blue-bordered cards give an immediate effect for spice; for example, “Seize Directorship” costs 7 spice (playtested at 8). Ongoing cards cost face-down Conspiracy chips. Each player starts with two starter chips, and each can fetch two more. The rulebook suggests keeping your total chip cost near 6. Once per game, the Imperial Keep token at Arrakeen lets you draw three Conspiracy cards and keep one. More diaries on raids and leaders are promised.

On Nov 2 the Dire Wolf shop listed “Dune: Imperium – Conspiracy (Pre-Order)” at $40.00 with U.S. and rest-of-world shipping both available. The shop also lists a Conspiracy Bundle – Dune: Imperium at $140 (regular $165) and a Conspiracy Bundle – Uprising at $120 (regular $140).

Sources: Dire Wolf Design Diary (Oct 26) · Dire Wolf shop · Bundle – Dune: Imperium · Bundle – Uprising

Dire Wolf: “Conspiracy is Coming Soon!” Full rundown, and pre-orders on Dire Wolf’s shop from Oct 26

Oct 22, 2026 Older · still relevant

Dire Wolf’s Oct 22 post is the first detailed official look at Dune: Imperium – Conspiracy, an expansion for both Dune: Imperium and Uprising. It adds Conspiracy cards (drafted at setup and paid for with spice or Conspiracy chips), Raids (spend swords during your Reveal turn to conquer planets, with consequences for factions), and optional modules: Imperial Edicts, Stoneburners (a one-time reset of the Imperium row / raid tokens), Spy tokens for base Imperium, and a new Swordmaster space (8/6 Solari). Dire Wolf lists 6 new Leaders, 46 new Imperium cards, the return of Graft, and Overthrow Mode (Paul vs. two or three conspirators who pool their victory points).

The post says pre-orders open on Dire Wolf’s shop on Monday, Oct 26. At about 8:45 a.m. ET on Oct 26 the shop page still said “Pre-orders opening soon!”; pre-orders have since opened (see above). Pre-orders there include a Shadow Council promo card. Asmodee Deutschland lists the German release as late November 2026.

Sources: Dire Wolf (Oct 22) · Dire Wolf shop

Conspiracy expansion on Q4 2026 retail track; US preorders listing ~Oct 31–Nov 15

Announced Aug 24, 2026 Older · active preorders

ICv2 reported Dire Wolf’s Conspiracy expansion for Q4 2026 retail. It is compatible with both Dune: Imperium and Uprising, adding lasting Conspiracy cards, planet raids, Imperial Edicts, and asymmetric Overthrow Mode (one Emperor vs. two or three opponents). GameNerdz lists an expected release of Oct 31, 2026 at $40 (SKU DWD01024); Earlier checks had GameNerdz at Oct 31, Miniature Market at “November 2026”, and Atomic Empire at Nov 15. Dire Wolf has opened direct pre-orders (above) but has not given a day-level retail date. Dates may still move.

Sources: ICv2 · GameNerdz · Atomic Empire

Digital 4.1.0 adds online Reputation system (Sept 30)

Sept 30, 2026 Older · still relevant

Dire Wolf shipped Dune: Imperium Digital patch 4.1.0 with a Reputation system aimed at early leavers: players start at 30 Rep, gain Rep for finishing games (wins not required), lose Rep for leaving early, and can set lobby minimums. Rep below 0 blocks Ranked until rebuilt. The patch also includes gameplay, UI, mobile, and achievement fixes.

Source: Dire Wolf Digital

Dice Throne

Dice-battling heroes · Roxley / Dice Throne

Nexus Kickstarter closes at $2,236,007 from 15,611 backers; BackerKit pledge manager is next

Ended Nov 3, 2026 · page checked Nov 9 New this week

The Dice Throne Nexus campaign ran Oct 13 to Nov 3. On Nov 9 the Kickstarter page showed $2,236,007 pledged from 15,611 backers against a $50,000 goal. That is well above last year’s Vanguard campaign ($1,784,099). Trackers posted slightly lower totals right after the close (about $2.20M from about 15,300 backers), which is normal while late pledges settle.

Dice Throne’s campaign FAQ points backers to a BackerKit pledge manager for upgrades and add-ons; $1 backers can also pick limited add-ons there.

Sources: Kickstarter · Kickstarter FAQ · BackerKit · Tabletop Analytics

Nexus Kickstarter nears $2M from 13,600+ backers in its final two days, passing last year’s Vanguard total

Stats Nov 2, 2026 · ends Nov 3 (9 p.m. ET) Carried forward · last week

Kickstarter’s public stats at about 8:40 a.m. ET on Nov 2 showed $1,996,603 from 13,620 backers, up from $1,721,084 and 11,531 backers on Oct 26. That is now above the $1,784,099 that last year’s Vanguard campaign raised. Kickstarter’s board-games collection (Oct 29) described Nexus as the most-backed live board game campaign at that time.

The campaign closes at 2 a.m. UK time on Nov 4, which is 9 p.m. ET on Tuesday, Nov 3. A $1 pledge still gives pledge-manager access after the campaign ends.

Sources: Kickstarter · Kickstarter board-games collection · Tabletop Analytics · PledgeBox tracker

Dice Throne SAGAS: The Crimson Code revealed: story-driven co-op for 1–4 players

Oct 9, 2026 (Screen Rant exclusive) Older · still relevant

Screen Rant’s Oct 9 exclusive (not covered last week) introduced Dice Throne SAGAS, a new story-driven line that starts with The Crimson Code, part of the Nexus campaign. It is playable solo or with up to three others. The Mad King returns inside a VR world called the Nexus. Play runs across a comic-book-style booklet board in five acts with boss fights. New red and blue “byte” tokens replace a long list of separate status effects, and heroes level up at 10 XP. Existing heroes can be brought in. The designers say it draws on Adventures and Marvel Missions.

Source: Screen Rant (Oct 9)

2026 Rules Updates: “Buh, Bye!” returns to Organized Play; new timing rules from Jan 1, 2027

Oct 5, 2026 Older · still relevant

Dice Throne’s official blog (Oct 5, not covered last week) says the Instant Action card Buh, Bye!, banned in Organized Play since January 2025, will no longer be banned from the Age that begins in January 2027 and “must now be used in all Hero decks.” A set of clarified timing rules for interrupting Actions takes effect Jan 1, 2027. The post says the core rules and “Golden Rules” are unchanged and most standard games will not feel different.

Source: Dice Throne blog (Oct 5)
